title: Root Makefile — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #96 (dev-makefile), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: `make dev`'s cleanup (now `trap 'kill -TERM -$$bpid -$$fpid' EXIT INT TERM` in the `dev` recipe, resolved from the earlier blocking finding by starting each of `backend`/`frontend` via `setsid` in its own process group and dropping the extra `( ... )` subshell wrapper so the trap sits on the shell that's actually make's direct child) reliably cleans up `uvicorn`/`vite` for both an interactive-terminal Ctrl-C (verified: `setsid` + `kill -INT` on the negative PGID -- clean shutdown, no orphans, no bash crash) and a plain `kill -TERM <top-pid>` from another shell (verified: GNU Make forwards SIGTERM to its direct child, which runs the trap and kills both process groups -- ports free, `pgrep -fa 'uvicorn|vite'` empty). What's still unresolved: sending *SIGINT specifically* to only the top-level `make dev` PID (not SIGTERM, and not via a real terminal's whole-process-group delivery) does nothing -- GNU Make explicitly ignores SIGINT while a recipe's child is running (deferring to the terminal to deliver it to the whole foreground process group directly), so the forwarding this fix relies on for SIGTERM never happens for a bare SIGINT sent to just the top pid: `make dev` sits orphaned indefinitely, `uvicorn`/`vite` never receive anything (re-verified directly against the current code: reproduced the same hang, then cleaned up the orphaned processes manually). This is a documented GNU Make behavior (not something fixable from within the recipe's own trap/signal handling), so non-blocking as before -- worth documenting as a known limitation if `make dev` is ever expected to run under a supervisor that specifically sends SIGINT (most use SIGTERM by default, which already works).

README.md's "Quick start (Makefile)" section says "`make backend` (and `make dev`, which depends on it)" -- `make dev` doesn't actually declare `backend` as a Make prerequisite; it invokes `$(MAKE) backend` as a subprocess from within its own recipe. The described runtime behavior (the venv-missing error surfaces through `make dev` too) is correct, only the "depends on" phrasing overstates it as formal Make dependency terminology. Minor wording fix.
